data.name: EMN0001Title
data.value: Two enum members declare the same public name

data.name: EMN0001Message
data.value: Members '{0}' and '{1}' both declare the public name '{2}'; a public name must identify exactly one member

data.name: EMN0001Description
data.value: Two members declaring the same public name make the value impossible to resolve unambiguously.

data.name: EMN0002Title
data.value: The public name is not usable

data.name: EMN0002Message
data.value: Member '{0}' declares the public name '{1}', which {2}

data.name: EMN0002Description
data.value: An empty name, or a name padded with whitespace, cannot be sent reliably over HTTP.

data.name: EMN0003Message
data.value: Member '{0}' of '{1}' declares no public name, so its C# name '{0}' becomes part of the public API contract

data.name: EMN0003Description
data.value: Once an enum declares a contract, every member must declare its public name. A member left unannotated answers to its C# name, which puts an internal identifier in the public contract and makes renaming it a breaking change — exactly what declaring a contract is meant to prevent.

data.name: EMN0004Title
data.value: A public name on a [Flags] enum contains a comma

data.name: EMN0004Message
data.value: Member '{0}' declares the public name '{1}'; on a [Flags] enum a comma separates the values of a combination and cannot appear inside a name

data.name: EMN0004Description
data.value: System.Text.Json validates declared names when it builds a converter, and refuses a comma inside one on a [Flags] enum: "Flags enums must additionally not contain commas". Such an enum cannot be serialized at all, so this rule turns a run-time failure into a build error. On any other enum the serializer accepts a comma in a name, and so does this package.

data.name: EMN0005Title
data.value: A public name shadows the C# name of another member

data.name: EMN0005Message
data.value: Member '{0}' declares the public name '{1}', which is also the C# name of member '{2}' ignoring case; the two then answer to overlapping spellings, and which member a given spelling reaches cannot be read off the enum

data.name: EMN0005Description
data.value: Two members then answer to overlapping spellings, and the rule is not one a reader can apply. Where the declared name is spelled exactly like the C# name it shadows, Enum.GetNames order decides which member the spelling reaches, and the other can become unreachable altogether. Where the two differ only by case, each exact spelling reaches its own member and only a casing matching neither falls back. This matters most when EMN0003 has been turned off to allow partial contracts, where it is the only remaining protection.

data.name: EMN0006Title
data.value: The public name cannot travel on every input channel

data.name: EMN0006Message
data.value: Member '{0}' declares the public name '{1}', which contains {2} and is refused on {3}

data.name: EMN0006Description
data.value: The promise of one contract on every channel only holds for names every channel can carry. A slash is refused inside a route segment, and a line break or a character outside printable ASCII is refused in a header. Reported as a warning rather than an error because the failure depends on the channels an API actually binds from: a name refused only in a header is harmless in an API that never binds one.
